## Purpose and Runtime
XYZW Web Helper is a browser-based automation and monitoring client for the XYZW game. It manages multiple game tokens locally, communicates with game servers over encrypted BON-protocol WebSockets, displays game state, and executes individual or batch game tasks. The primary runtime is a Vue 3/Vite SPA with Pinia state; a separate Python service optionally hosts `.bin` files and issues token URLs.

Entry points: `src/main.js`, `src/App.vue`, `src/router/index.js`.

## Application Shell and Navigation
The SPA bootstraps Vue, global styling, stores, and route-driven feature views. `DefaultLayout` provides the shared authenticated application frame; routes separate login/token-import flows from dashboards, daily tasks, batch automation, role management, legion war, and profile views. Route metadata/guards form the boundary preventing token-dependent pages from running without an imported role.

Paths: `src/main.js`, `src/router/index.js`, `src/layout/DefaultLayout.vue`.

## Token and Role Lifecycle
Token import supports manual, URL, and `.bin`-derived inputs. Token stores own the selected role, persisted credentials, refresh metadata, and connection association; role state captures game-facing identity and status. Browser persistence is the core security boundary: game credentials are intended to remain client-side, with IndexedDB available for durable local data.

Paths: `src/views/TokenImport/index.vue`, `src/stores/tokenStore.ts`, `src/stores/gameRoles.js`.

## Game Transport and Protocol Boundary
The transport layer converts game commands into BON payloads, applies supported encryption/encoding formats, and sends them through WebSocket clients. It handles connection lifecycle, message routing, queues, and reconnect behavior. Incoming messages are decoded and propagated into event-specific Pinia stores, separating opaque server protocol traffic from UI-facing game state.

Paths: `src/utils/bonProtocol.js`, `src/utils/xyzwWebSocket.js`, `src/stores/events/index.ts`.

## State Projection and Feature UI
Feature views compose card and domain components around reactive stores: dashboard/status, daily activities, team, towers, clubs, rankings, and legion war. Event stores partition server updates by concern—role, activity, tower, team, chat, hangup, study, legion, and clock—so UI components consume normalized live state rather than direct socket traffic.

Paths: `src/views/Dashboard.vue`, `src/views/DailyTasks.vue`, `src/stores/events/role.ts`.

## Automation Execution
Automation is command-driven rather than server-hosted. Single-task runners coordinate helper/daily actions, while the batch subsystem schedules and executes task families such as arena, bottle, car, dungeon, hang-up, items, store, and tower. It relies on the shared command/connection layer, making WebSocket availability and token validity prerequisites for automation.

Paths: `src/utils/helperTaskRunner.js`, `src/utils/dailyTaskRunner.js`, `src/utils/batch/index.js`.

## Deployment and Optional Services
The frontend builds to static assets and can run behind Cloudflare Pages. `worker.js` is the edge/API proxy boundary; `wrangler.toml` configures its Cloudflare runtime. Docker packaging includes Nginx for static delivery. The optional Python backend, declared under `server/requirements.txt`, provides authenticated multi-user `.bin` storage and token-URL retrieval; it is separate from normal local-token operation.

Paths: `worker.js`, `wrangler.toml`, `server/requirements.txt`.
